title: Building Protected MCP Servers — Den Delimarsky and Julia Kasper, MCP Steering Committee & Microsoft
talk_summary: The talk explains the new MCP authorization spec, which separates the MCP resource server from the authorization server so developers don't have to build their own token factory. It demos a C# SDK and Azure API Management gateway that handle OAuth discovery, consent, and token validation with minimal boilerplate.

takeaways.technique: Delegate auth to an external identity provider via protected-resource metadata
takeaways.what_they_do: The MCP server returns HTTP 401 with a Protected Resource Metadata document pointing at an external authorization server; the client does the OAuth dance and the server only validates tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the server now doesn't actually need to manage tokens. You only need to make sure that you're validating them

takeaways.technique: Gateway in front of remote MCP servers
takeaways.what_they_do: Put an API gateway (Azure API Management) between clients and the MCP server to centralize auth, consent, logging, and monitoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I always recommend putting a gateway in between to make it more secure and actually use it to protect

takeaways.technique: Auto-generate MCP tools from existing REST endpoints
takeaways.what_they_do: Platform converts existing REST APIs into remote MCP tools so agents can call them without bespoke wrappers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can now also start transforming your REST APIs into remote MCP servers using our tools
